preamble: The glottal fricative [h] can be reinterpreted as the velar fricative [x] when a language or dialect merges the two or lacks [h]. In Spanish, words with the Old Spanish aspirate [h] (from Latin f-) that entered the standard through Andalusian speech, where aspirated h had merged with the velar j, now have /x/ (jolgorio < holgorio, juerga beside huelga); Russian, which has no /h/, regularly renders foreign [h] as х [x] (хобби 'hobby').

examples.note: Andalusian-type pronunciation with the aspirate merged into /x/ was adopted into the standard.
Doublet of huelga 'strike', from an Andalusian pronunciation.
